threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local Word-document processing engine providing Rust byte APIs, a native CLI, PyO3/Python interfaces, WASM interfaces, an npm CLI, and a stdio MCP server. Document packages, XML, legacy DOC data, embedded media, Markdown and edit plans cross into parsers and transformations; results return as bytes or are published to host files. The MCP adapter grants a persistent directory capability for explicit document reads and output publication. Native rendering additionally consumes ambient font resources and maintains a font index. Optional self-update and maintainer publication workflows introduce separate network, executable replacement and registry authority. findings.title: Rendering a renamed XML story bypasses depth admission and can abort the host
findings.summary: A document author can point a header or footer relationship at a non-.xml internal part containing deeply nested XML. Admission skips XML policy for that filename, but rendering recursively parses the part and can exhaust the process stack.

severity.rationale: Attacker-supplied document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering host with a small input; no remote service exposure is assumed. Process CPU/memory limits do not prevent a per-process stack-overflow abort.
severity.changeConditions: Isolated disposable conversion processes reduce the application-level impact; a shared conversion service would increase impact.

confidence.rationale: Static source trace establishes the filename-only gate, main-only fallback, relationship-selected bytes and unbounded recursive parser. No runtime exploit was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Caller-controlled package reaches layout
codeEvidence.explanation: `docx_to_pdf` and PNG/report paths share `with_layout`; the package is admitted and opened before header processing.

codeEvidence.label: Admission chooses policy by suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: The inflated part receives XML policy checks only when its name ends in .xml or .rels. An internal header.bin is counted in byte budgets but skipped by XML policy.

codeEvidence.label: Only the main document gets a second check
codeEvidence.explanation: The explicit fallback protects a renamed main part; it does not validate other relationship-selected XML consumers.

codeEvidence.label: Header reference selected from the document
codeEvidence.explanation: An attacker-controlled section reference selects a relationship ID passed to `load_chrome_part`.

codeEvidence.label: Arbitrary internal target read as XML
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected target bytes are decoded as UTF-8 and forwarded to `chrome_part_xml` without a policy check.

codeEvidence.label: Header/footer raw parser
codeEvidence.explanation: `chrome_part_xml` directly invokes the recursive infallible DOM parser on bytes skipped by the admission XML checks.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship controls target path
codeEvidence.explanation: The document relationship ID selects the package target without a filename-extension or content-type restriction.

codeEvidence.label: DOM nesting consumes call stack
codeEvidence.explanation: Each nested element recurses into `parse_element`; this path has no depth budget, so sufficiently deep XML exhausts the host stack.

rootCause.summary: The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant.

findings.remediation: Enforce the active XML policy before parsing every XML relationship target irrespective of extension, or enumerate typed XML parts during admission. Make the raw DOM parser iterative or depth-bounded as defense in depth.

counterEvidence: Normal .xml/.rels parts receive XML checks, and renamed main documents are explicitly rechecked.
Raw parse_xdocument is documented as unchecked; the defect is its use behind a supposedly admitted package boundary, not the existence of that API.
External relationships are not needed; this exploit uses internal package bytes.
limitations: No application code or malicious input was executed; exact crash depth depends on platform and stack size.
validation.summary: Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> with_layout -> admit -> suffix-based XML check skips header.bin -> internal relationship resolution -> chrome_part_xml -> recursive parse_element -> stack exhaustion

impact.rationale: Host-process availability; no confidentiality, arbitrary file write or code-execution claim.

likelihood.rationale: Default parser path accepts the internally linked renamed payload; deep nesting is directly attacker-controlled.

reachability.summary: A document author needs only to have the consumer render the supplied package; no operator configuration change, filesystem access or network access is needed.
reachability.outcome: rendering process abort or equivalent stack exhaustion

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX with an ordinary main part, a section headerReference, an internal header relationship targeting header.bin, and a deeply nested well-formed XML payload at that target; render via the public PDF/PNG APIs or their wrappers.

remediationTests: An internal header/footer target named .bin with nesting above max_xml_depth must return INVALID_XML before DOM construction.
Repeat with custom part names and raised/lowered InputLimits; ordinary shallow parts must remain supported.

originalCandidates.message: Confirmed candidate: admission scans XML policy only when archive entry lower.ends_with('.xml'|'.rels') (src/admission.rs:534-545), special-cases only main_part missing extension (558-569). Renderer loads arbitrary header/footer relationship target without extension constraint (src/convert/mod.rs:20762-20779), passes directly to unbounded recursive Dom::parse_xdocument at 20794-20795; parse_element recursively invokes itself at src/xmllinq/parse.rs:660-662. An attacker can target word/header.bin and put deeply nested well-formed XML there, bypass max_xml_depth=256 and crash converter host via stack exhaustion. Investigating all entrypoint controls before final.

findings.title: Reading a small legacy DOC can expand repeated text pieces into billions of characters
findings.summary: A legacy DOC author can reuse the same physical WordDocument text range in many contiguous logical pieces. `main_text` expands every logical character into `StoryChar` without a decoded-character budget, exhausting host memory or CPU.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled parser input can deny availability through disproportionate work or allocation in default public paths. Impact is process availability with high likelihood for a crafted input; no remote exposure, confidentiality loss or code execution is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A disposable process with strict CPU/memory budgets reduces application-level impact; shared long-lived processing increases it.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source trace confirms the input-to-sink control gap and strongest counterevidence; no application or exploit execution was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Public legacy reader
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-supplied streams provide the FIB and piece table passed directly to main_text.

codeEvidence.label: Physical offsets and logical ranges
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker CP endpoints and fc offsets become pieces; separate pieces may retain the same physical offset.

codeEvidence.label: Coverage without expansion budget
codeEvidence.explanation: Increasing contiguous logical ranges pass without constraining their total decoded length.

codeEvidence.label: Expand every logical character
codeEvidence.explanation: Each logical CP derives an in-bounds physical offset and is decoded even when earlier pieces already referenced those bytes.

codeEvidence.label: Retain expanded characters
codeEvidence.explanation: The decoder pushes a new StoryChar for every logical character without an output budget.

codeEvidence.label: CLI routes OLE to converter
codeEvidence.explanation: OLE input reaches doc_to_docx before the later DOCX sniff/admission path.

rootCause.summary: `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

findings.remediation: Apply a configurable maximum decoded-character/output-byte budget before expansion and during emission; refuse excessive logical story length even when repeated physical ranges are individually valid.

counterEvidence: CFB sector-chain iteration is bounded by file size and invalid CP coverage is rejected.
No deployment exposure or measured allocation size is assumed; the exact StoryChar layout is platform dependent.
limitations: Static-only validation; no runtime measurement or deployed embedding assessment.
validation.summary: Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

dataflow.summary: legacy DOC bytes -> CompoundFile streams/FIB -> pieces -> main_text logical CP iteration -> StoryChar vector -> memory/CPU exhaustion

impact.rationale: CPU, memory or stack availability of the consuming process.

likelihood.rationale: The default source path accepts the required attacker-controlled representation without a bound on the demonstrated expansion.

reachability.summary: supplier of a legacy .doc consumed by legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown or doc_to_docx can trigger the affected public input path without changing trusted configuration.
reachability.attacker: supplier of a legacy .doc consumed by legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown or doc_to_docx
reachability.outcome: Process unavailability or failed conversion through resource exhaustion

attackPath.summary: A legacy DOC author can reuse the same physical WordDocument text range in many contiguous logical pieces. `main_text` expands every logical character into `StoryChar` without a decoded-character budget, exhausting host memory or CPU.

remediationTests: A valid piece table with increasing CPs but many references to one short physical range must return a resource-limit error before allocating proportional to its claimed story.
Preserve legitimate repeated/fast-save pieces within the configured decoded-text limit.

originalCandidate.message: Distinct source-backed candidate: legacy DOC piece-table amplification. legacy_doc::read at180-197 calls pieces then main_text with attacker FIB ccp_text, no InputLimits. main_text1154-1183 only validates increasing contiguous CP coverage, then1191-1222 loops each CP and pushes StoryChar; repeated pieces may point to same WordDocument byte range (fc unrestricted except per-byte get). CompoundFile chain caps are input-sized but do not bound this logical expansion. CLI convert src/bin/jubarte.rs3129-3131 routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx. findings.title: Opening duplicate relationship records performs quadratic repair work
findings.summary: A DOCX author can include many distinct relationship IDs, each repeated identically. The package loader retains these records for repair, and each duplicate scans the growing repaired-ID vector, causing quadratic CPU work within normal archive limits.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled parser input can deny availability through disproportionate work or allocation in default public paths. Impact is process availability with high likelihood for a crafted input; no remote exposure, confidentiality loss or code execution is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A disposable process with strict CPU/memory budgets reduces application-level impact; shared long-lived processing increases it.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source trace confirms the input-to-sink control gap and strongest counterevidence; no application or exploit execution was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Metadata retains all records
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker-controlled relationship list is retained for later duplicate repair.

codeEvidence.label: Every relationship set is repaired
codeEvidence.explanation: Opening the package runs duplicate repair on both package and part relationship sets.

codeEvidence.label: Linear scan for every new duplicate
codeEvidence.explanation: Identical duplicate IDs bypass conflicting-record refusal and scan every previously repaired ID.

rootCause.summary: `read_relationships` preserves the record list and `PartFs::open_within` invokes `drop_repeated_relationships`. Its `seen` map finds duplicates efficiently, but each duplicate then uses `repaired.contains` over all previously repaired IDs. Repeating each of N distinct IDs twice requires roughly N(N-1)/2 string comparisons.

findings.remediation: Track repaired IDs in a HashSet while retaining a Vec only for ordered output, and optionally bound total metadata records.

counterEvidence: Conflicting records under one ID are refused, but the attack uses identical pairs.
XML byte budgets bound input size, yet permit many records and do not bound quadratic work; process CPU limits can contain external impact.
limitations: Static-only validation; no runtime measurement or deployed embedding assessment.
validation.summary: Metadata parsing preserves duplicate IDs (`rels.items = items`), and identical duplicates are intentionally repaired rather than rejected. A large shallow .rels fits XML depth/tag/byte caps and uses only one ZIP entry; max_entries limits ZIP members, not relationship records. No record-count bound precedes the vector scan.

dataflow.summary: attacker .rels records -> read_relationships items -> PartFs::open_within -> drop_repeated_relationships -> growing Vec::contains scan -> CPU exhaustion

impact.rationale: CPU, memory or stack availability of the consuming process.

likelihood.rationale: The default source path accepts the required attacker-controlled representation without a bound on the demonstrated expansion.

taxonomy.category: Unbounded allocation from numeric table metadata

codeEvidence.label: Cell span accepts arbitrary usize
codeEvidence.explanation: The numeric XML value becomes a colspan with a minimum only and no upper bound.

codeEvidence.label: Row skips accept arbitrary usize
codeEvidence.explanation: Positive gridBefore/gridAfter counts become span metadata without an upper bound.

codeEvidence.label: Unchecked occupancy sizes column vector
codeEvidence.explanation: The sum of attacker spans becomes the vector length independently of XML byte limits.

codeEvidence.label: Merge tracking repeats allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: Per-column merge tracking grows to col+span from the same numeric metadata.

rootCause.summary: `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.

findings.remediation: Validate a practical total grid-column limit before accumulating or allocating, apply it to spans and skipped columns, and use checked arithmetic with typed refusal.

counterEvidence: Malformed/non-numeric attributes fall back safely; the exploit uses a valid numeric value.
Default XML attribute-width and archive budgets accept the small input. Native memory limits or a WASM heap cap constrain the host impact to failed/terminated conversion.
limitations: Static-only validation; no runtime measurement or deployed embedding assessment.
validation.summary: A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.

dataflow.summary: DOCX table attributes -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell colspan -> occupancy -> cols vec/resize and merge open.resize -> allocation failure
